lessons.title: durch, für, gegen, ohne, um
lessons.summary: Five prepositions are always followed by the accusative. Remember them as DOGFU.

cards.title: When do you need them?
cards.body: Moving through a town and describing your flat: **Gehen Sie durch den Park.** **Die Post ist um die Ecke.** **Das Regal ist für das Wohnzimmer.**

examples.english: We're walking through the park.

cards.title: The five: DOGFU
cards.body: **durch** (through), **ohne** (without), **gegen** (against / around a time), **für** (for), **um** (around / at a time). After them: **den, einen, meinen** for masculine.
cards.tip: DOGFU: Durch, Ohne, Gegen, Für, Um.

cards.title: Only masculine changes
cards.body: As always in the accusative, only masculine changes: **der → den**, **ein → einen**. Pronouns: **für mich, für dich, für ihn, ohne uns**.

examples.english: The flowers are for you.
The car drives into a tree.

cards.title: Short forms
cards.body: In speech: **durch das → durchs**, **für das → fürs**, **um das → ums**.

examples.english: Go around the house.

cards.title: Common mistakes
cards.body: Don't use dative endings after these five: not 'für dem Kind' but **für das Kind**; not 'durch dem Park' but **durch den Park**; not 'ohne einem Plan' but **ohne einen Plan**.

examples.german: Ich suche eine Wohnung **für meinen** Sohn.
examples.english: I'm looking for a flat for my son.

games.prompt: Gehen Sie ___ Park bis zur Kirche.
games.english: Walk through the park to the church.
games.explanation: durch + accusative: der Park → den Park.

games.prompt: Match the preposition and its meaning

games.explanation: durch, ohne, gegen, für, um → accusative; mit, zu, bei → dative.

lessons.title: aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu
lessons.summary: These prepositions are always followed by the dative: dem, der, dem, den + n.

cards.title: When do you need them?
cards.body: Asking the way and talking about where you live: **Wie komme ich zum Bahnhof?** **Ich wohne bei meinen Eltern.** **Der Bus fährt vom Rathaus zur Uni.**

examples.german: Fahren Sie **mit der** Linie 5 **bis zum** Markt.
examples.english: Take line 5 to the market.

cards.title: The list
cards.body: **aus** (out of, from), **bei** (at, near), **mit** (with), **nach** (to, after), **seit** (since, for), **von** (from, of), **zu** (to), **gegenüber** (opposite).

examples.english: The pharmacy is opposite the station.
I've been living here for a year.

cards.title: Dative forms
cards.body: der/das → **dem**, die → **der**, plural → **den** + n. Short forms: **zum, zur, beim, vom**.

cards.title: Asking the way
cards.body: **Entschuldigung, wie komme ich zum/zur …?** – **Gehen Sie geradeaus bis zur Ampel, dann links.**

examples.english: How do I get to the library?
Go as far as the crossroads.

cards.title: Common mistakes
cards.body: Not 'zu der Bahnhof': **zum** Bahnhof. Not 'mit die Kinder': **mit den Kindern**. Not 'seit ein Jahr': **seit einem Jahr**.

examples.english: I cycle to work.

games.explanation: zu dem → zum (der/das), zu der → zur (die).
Wo? at someone's place: bei + dative (meiner).

lessons.title: Wo or wohin?
lessons.summary: Nine prepositions take the dative for a position (wo?) and the accusative for a direction (wohin?).

cards.title: When do you need them?
cards.body: Describing your flat and moving things: **Das Bild hängt an der Wand.** **Ich hänge das Bild an die Wand.** **Wir wohnen in der Stadt, wir ziehen in die Stadt.**

examples.english: The cat is lying on the sofa.
The cat jumps onto the sofa.

cards.title: The nine
cards.body: **in** (in), **an** (at, on a vertical surface), **auf** (on top of), **über** (above), **unter** (under), **vor** (in front of), **hinter** (behind), **neben** (next to), **zwischen** (between).

examples.german: Der Tisch steht **zwischen dem** Sofa und **dem** Fenster.
examples.english: The table is between the sofa and the window.

cards.title: Wo? → dative, Wohin? → accusative
cards.body: A **position** (no change of place) → **dative**. A **movement** to a new place → **accusative**.
cards.tip: Wohin has the -n of the accusative (den), wo has -m of the dative (dem).

cards.title: Short forms
cards.body: **in dem → im**, **in das → ins**, **an dem → am**, **an das → ans**.

examples.german: Ich gehe **ins** Bad. – Ich bin **im** Bad.
examples.english: I'm going into the bathroom. – I'm in the bathroom.

cards.title: Common mistakes
cards.body: Walking around inside a room is still **wo**: **Ich gehe im Park spazieren** (dative). Only a move **into** a new place is wohin: **Ich gehe in den Park**.

examples.english: Put the phone on the table!

games.prompt: Ich stelle die Lampe neben ___ Sofa.
games.english: I'm putting the lamp next to the sofa.

games.prompt: Match the preposition and its meaning
games.explanation: Four of the nine two-way prepositions.

lessons.topic: Verbs for positions and directions (Verben für Positionen und Richtungen)
lessons.title: stellen/stehen, legen/liegen…
lessons.summary: German says not just 'put' and 'be', but how: standing, lying, sitting or hanging. Each verb comes in a pair.

cards.title: When do you need them?
cards.body: Furnishing a flat and saying where things are: **Wohin stelle ich den Schrank? – Der Schrank steht schon im Flur.** English uses 'put' and 'is'; German chooses by shape.

examples.english: The book is (lying) on the table.

cards.title: The pairs
cards.body: Action (**wohin?**, accusative, regular verb) vs result (**wo?**, dative, irregular verb).

rows: flat things: books, phones, people in bed

cards.tip: The action verbs have e (stellen, legen, setzen); the result verbs mostly have i/ie (liegen, sitzen).

cards.title: Action: wohin + accusative
cards.body: Someone moves something to a place: **regular** verb + **accusative**.

examples.english: I put the vase on the table.
He hangs the jacket on the hook.

cards.title: Result: wo + dative
cards.body: Something is already there: **irregular** verb + **dative**.

examples.english: The vase is on the table.
The jacket is hanging on the hook.

cards.title: Common mistakes
cards.body: Not 'Das Buch steht auf dem Tisch' (unless it's upright): it **liegt**. Not 'Ich liege das Handy': **Ich lege das Handy** hin. Bottles and glasses **stehen**.

examples.english: The children are already sitting at the table.

games.explanation: Action verbs take the accusative, result verbs the dative.

games.prompt: Match the action and the result
games.explanation: Each action has its result verb.

games.english: The phone is (lying) on the sofa.
games.explanation: A flat thing already there: liegen + dative.
